newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania gearing for big boost in tourism industry.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania gearing for big boost in tourism industry.

text.p: Tanzania is aiming for 500,000 tourist arrivals by the year 2000 and hopes to attract higher spending visitors, the Tanzania Tourist Board (TTB) said on Thursday.

TTB spokeswoman Annette Rust said 293,834 tourists came to Tanzania in 1995, earning the East African country an estimated $258 million, up from 261,595 tourists in 1994 who contributed about $192.10 million.
The board forecasts over 326,000 arrivals this year, bringing earnings over $322 million.
The industry has seen growth since economic reforms started in 1986 when 103,361 tourist arrivals were recorded.
Tanzania has set as a priority the development of a viable tourism industry targeting high class, high-spending tourists.

"We're aiming for the high to middle class tourists. It's better to have a few that spend a lot rather than a lot spending a little -- besides its better that way for protecting the environment," Rust told Reuters.
She saw infrastructure development as one of the problems.

The Selous game reserve in the south, one of the country's newest tourist attractions covering a largely uninhabited area the size of Switzerland, suffers from a particularly acute lack of infrastucture.

"Infrastructure up to now is not up to standard. The southern circuit especially. There are no communications in that area -- they (tourist lodges) use radios but even with these there are difficulties," Rust said.
